description:
The World’s Most Popular Track Cycling Chainring – Trusted by Amateurs and Pros Alike

The Miche Primato Advanced Track Chainring is the most widely used chainring in track cycling, chosen by thousands of amateur riders worldwide and trusted by elite professionals, including the Italian National Team with stars like Filippo Ganna and Jonathan Milan. Its combination of affordability, reliability, and aerodynamic performance makes it the go-to chainring for riders at every level, from club racers to professionals.

Why the Chainring Matters in Track Cycling

In track cycling, the chainring is the critical first link in the drivetrain, transferring every watt of rider power into the chain. A stiffer, more precise chainring ensures:

Maximum efficiency
– reduced articulation losses, smoother chain engagement.

Consistent power transfer
– vital for explosive sprinting or sustained pursuit efforts.

Aerodynamic advantage
– streamlined profiles reduce drag around the crank and bottom bracket.

As covered in our
Chainrings & Sprockets Guide
, even small improvements in drivetrain stiffness and efficiency can make the difference between victory and second place.

Key Features at a Glance

CNC-Machined Aluminium Construction
– precision-engineered for stiffness and consistency.

Aerodynamic Profile
– smoother airflow around the chainring-crank interface.

Proven at the Highest Level
– used by the Italian National Team, including Olympic and World Champions.

Wide Size Range (46T–68T)
– covers every event, from endurance to sprint disciplines.

Seigiorni Branding
– sizes 59–63 carry “Miche Seigiorni,” while 64+ feature “Seigiorni Oro.”

BCD:
144 mm (standard for track cycling).

Chain Compatibility:
1/8".

Finish:
Black anodised with laser-etched graphics.

Mechanical Efficiency & Performance

Stiff aluminium structure prevents flex, even under high sprint torque (>2000W).

Larger sizes (60T+) help reduce chain articulation losses, improving drivetrain efficiency by 1–2 watts compared to smaller chainrings.

Optimised tooth profile for precise chain engagement and durability.

Event Suitability

Sprint / Keirin / Kilo
– oversized options (60T–68T) deliver stiffness and reduced drivetrain losses.

Individual & Team Pursuit
– widely used by pursuit specialists, including Ganna and Milan.

Points, Scratch, Madison
– versatile sizing makes it a popular choice for bunch racing.

Amateur Racing & Training
– outstanding value and long-term durability for club riders.

For amateur riders, it remains the best balance of cost, performance, and availability.

Compatibility & Setup

Fits all 144 BCD cranksets: Shimano Dura-Ace 7710, Rotor ALDHU, Miche Pistard, FSA Vision, etc.

The Olympic Champion’s Choice – Maximum Stiffness, Minimum Loss

The Digirit Carbon Track Chainring is the chainring trusted by the world’s fastest riders — including the Netherlands national team and many of the medallists at both the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games.

With its revolutionary full-carbon construction, it has rapidly become the benchmark for elite track cycling, replacing traditional steel and alloy rings as the ultimate power-transfer link in the drivetrain.

Engineered for stiffness, precision, and weight savings, the Digirit Carbon Track Chainring has been awarded multiple Design & Innovation Awards and is now the most widely used chainring at the very top of the sport.

Why Chainrings Matter in Track Cycling

The chainring is the first point of power transfer, converting raw leg torque into chain tension.

Larger chainrings improve efficiency by reducing articulation losses — typically saving 1–2 watts at 60T+ sizes compared to smaller options.

Chainring stiffness is critical: under sprint loads exceeding 2,000 watts, even minor flex can waste power or compromise chainline.

Digirit’s carbon architecture delivers unmatched stiffness-to-weight, ensuring every watt counts.

Carbon layup engineered for zero deflection, even under explosive sprint torque.

Smooth, consistent tooth profile ensures precise chain engagement at all cadences.

Aerodynamics & CdA

Larger carbon chainrings create a cleaner airflow around the bottom bracket area, reducing drag.

Carbon’s structural properties allow for thinner aero-optimised tooth bases without compromising stiffness.

Proven in wind tunnel testing and validated by Olympic medal-winning performances.

Inspect teeth regularly — although carbon is exceptionally stiff, precise chain fit is critical at elite levels.

Frequently Asked Questions – Digirit Carbon Track Chainring

Why do professional track cyclists use carbon chainrings?

Carbon chainrings like the Digirit Carbon Track Chainring deliver the highest stiffness-to-weight ratio, ensuring zero flex under loads of 2000+ watts. They also improve drivetrain efficiency and aerodynamics, which is why they were the most used chainrings at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.

Are larger chainrings faster in track cycling?

Yes. Larger chainrings reduce chain articulation losses, typically saving 1–2 watts compared to smaller chainrings. This is why professional riders often use oversized chainrings (60T and above) in sprint and pursuit events.

Is the Digirit Carbon Track Chainring compatible with my crankset?

The Digirit Carbon Track Chainring uses the standard 144 BCD fitting, making it compatible with leading track cranksets including Shimano Dura-Ace 7710, Rotor ALDHU Track, Miche Pistard, and FSA Vision Track models.

Which events is the Digirit Carbon Track Chainring best for?

The Digirit Carbon Track Chainring is suitable for all elite-level track events, including Sprint, Keirin, Kilo, Individual & Team Pursuit, Madison, and Points races.

What chain should I use with the Digirit Carbon Track Chainring?

For maximum efficiency and strength, pair it with a professional 1/8" track chain such as the Izumi Kai, DID Midas, or Renold Track Chain — the same chains trusted by Olympic teams worldwide.

The Sugino ZEN is one of the most iconic and trusted track chainrings ever produced. Manufactured in Japan to exceptionally tight tolerances, the ZEN delivers the precision, stiffness, and reliability demanded by elite sprint and pursuit programmes worldwide.

Whether you are building a world-class sprint bike, refining a pursuit drivetrain, or upgrading your current setup for cleaner, quieter, more efficient performance, the Sugino ZEN remains one of the most dependable 144BCD chainrings available.

Precision-machined aluminium construction

Extremely tight tolerances for highly accurate tooth geometry

Excellent stiffness under maximal sprint torque

Consistent chainline and circularity for smoother, quieter running

Proven across elite sprint, keirin, kilo, team sprint, pursuit, and bunch events

Long-term reliability, ideal for daily training and world-class racing

144BCD bolt pattern for standard track cranksets

Why Chainrings Matter in Track Cycling

The chainring is the first point of power transfer, converting raw leg torque into chain tension.

Larger chainrings improve efficiency by reducing articulation losses — typically saving 1–2 watts at 60T+ sizes compared to smaller options.

Sugino ZEN Chainring FAQs

Is the Sugino ZEN still used at elite level?
Yes. Despite the rise of carbon chainrings, the ZEN continues to be used by national teams and professional riders who value its stiffness, reliability, and proven tolerances.

What thickness chain does it support?
The ZEN is optimised for 1/8 inch track chains.

Is this suitable for high-torque sprint events?
Absolutely. Its stiffness and precision machining make it ideal for match sprint, keirin, kilo, and team sprint applications.

Does the ZEN help reduce chain noise?
Chain noise is almost always caused by poor chainline. However, the ZENs precision machining provides a clean, accurate interface which supports quieter running when combined with correct chainline.

The ZEN is available in a broad range of tooth counts 50 to 70, allowing very precise gear-inch configurations across sprint and endurance disciplines.
